passage:
Tuesday: At lunch the friends planned a film for Sunday. Uday said he had homework, again. His face felt hot. He had been dodging paid plans for a month, ashamed of the reason.

Friday: He stayed after robotics club and, before he could stop himself, told Pooja, the lab mentor, everything. Pooja did not pity him. "Do you know how many people can't stretch a budget? You've been doing it all month. That's a skill." Uday laughed, surprised.

Next Wednesday: At the bench he told Yash, his closest friend, "We're saving money at home, so I skip paid things. Free stuff is fine." Yash shrugged. "Then let's do the park match Sunday." The hot feeling did not come back.

qa.q: On which day did Uday tell Pooja?
qa.a: Uday told Pooja on Friday, after robotics club.

qa.q: How did Uday feel when he said he had homework again, and why?
qa.a: Uday felt embarrassed and hot in the face, because he was ashamed of the money reason.

qa.q: What other approach could Uday try with the friends, and why?
qa.a: Uday could suggest free plans first, like a park match, because that lets him join without hiding the reason.

qa.q: How does Yash respond, and what might that mean for Yash?
qa.a: Yash shrugs and suggests the park match, which suggests it never mattered to Yash and that the friendship holds.

grounding: The teen first feels embarrassed before friends, and after talking with a mentor begins to see careful handling of limited money as a skill and shares openly with one close friend.

passage: Hrithik, you've been hiding that you can't go on the trip? Sit. Your Francis Uncle has a story. In Class 11, after my father's shop shut, I was so ashamed. I wore my shoes till the soles flapped and told everyone I liked them broken in. I skipped every outing with some excuse. My football coach, Mr D'Costa, noticed. One evening he asked why I'd stopped coming to team dinners. I told him, eyes on the ground. He said, "Francis, you know how to make one pair of shoes last three years, and cook for your brothers on almost nothing. That's a skill. Most grown men can't do it." I had never thought of it like that. The next week I told my best friend, Joe, the truth. He just said, "Okay. Then we'll eat at my place."

qa.q: What excuse did young Francis give for his shoes?
qa.a: That he liked them broken in.

qa.q: How did young Francis feel before talking to Mr D'Costa?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and embarrassed, hiding the truth behind excuses and skipping outings.

qa.q: Which moment in the story changed how Francis saw himself, and why?
qa.a: Mr D'Costa naming his careful handling of very little money as a skill, which turned shame into pride in being resourceful.

qa.q: How did Joe react when Francis told him?
qa.a: Joe was calm and kind, simply offering to eat at his place, showing the truth didn't change the friendship.

grounding: An elder recalls a mentor helping him see careful handling of limited money as a skill, after which he told one close friend.

passage: Pema had three days to reply to Tashi's birthday invitation, a bowling party everyone was going to, and no money for the entry or a gift since his mother's shop closed in the winter. He had already lied twice that week about "having tuition". His face burned every time someone mentioned the party. On Wednesday Hemant Sir, who ran the science club, found him alone in the lab at lunch. Pema ended up telling him everything. Hemant Sir listened, then said, "You've been running your family's grocery list in your head for months, haven't you? You know what everything costs and what lasts longest. That's not something to hide. That's a skill." Pema hadn't seen it like that. That evening he messaged Tashi, only Tashi: "Can't do bowling, things are tight at home. Can I bring you a card I made?" Tashi replied: "Obviously. Come for cake after."

qa.q: What kind of party was Tashi having?
How did Pema feel whenever someone mentioned the party?
qa.a: His face burned, so he felt embarrassed and ashamed about not being able to afford it.

qa.q: What did Pema do that shows the new way of seeing things?
qa.a: He told Tashi honestly and offered a handmade card, handling the tight situation openly instead of hiding behind excuses.

qa.q: How does Tashi respond to Pema's honesty?
qa.a: Tashi responds warmly, inviting him for cake, showing the friendship doesn't depend on money 🤍.

grounding: Shows a teen, after talking with a mentor, reframing his careful handling of little money as a skill and telling one close friend.
